title:
A seventh gravedigger came beside Mr Bloom to take up an idle spade.
 
 —O, excuse me!
 
 He stepped aside nimbly.
html_source:
For Bloom to be standing next to an idle spade is significant. In Judaism, it is customary for the community to bury the dead – to take up shovels themselves and cover the coffin. It is the very definition of a “Mitzvah” – a final act of kindness that can never be returned. At a Jewish funeral, this custom is ritualized; it’s highly unlikely that Bloom would not be aware of it.

“He stepped aside nimbly”. Stepping away from the shovel in this context is symbolic.
